title: GSTA1 depletes glutathione and exacerbates oxidative stress in alpha-Amanitin-induced hepatotoxicity.
authors: Liu, Tao; Zhang, Xu; Zhang, Wei; Yang, Dejin; Li, Jipeng; Liu, Lin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究alpha-Amanitin与GSTA1蛋白的相互作用及氧化应激肝毒性机制，虽含分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: alpha-Amanitin (alpha-AMA), the principal toxin of lethal mushrooms, induces severe liver injury by exacerbating oxidative stress. Glutathione S-transferase A1 (GSTA1), a crucial hepatic antioxidant enzyme, plays an ambiguous role in this process. METHODS: A mouse model of alpha-AMA-induced liver injury was established. Hepatic damage was assessed via serum biochemistry (ALT, AST, T-BIL) and histopathology (H&E staining). Oxidative stress markers (SOD, CAT, MDA) were measured. Integrated transcriptomics and metabolomics were employed to identify critical pathways. The interaction between alpha-AMA and GSTA1 was evaluated using molecular docking and Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) assays. In vitro mechanisms were further dissected in HUH7 cells using siRNA knockdown, and functional rescue experiments. RESULTS: alpha-AMA caused significant liver injury, evidenced by elevated serum markers, worsened histopathology, and increased oxidative stress (reduced SOD/CAT, elevated MDA). Multi-omics analysis pinpointed GSTA1 and glutathione metabolism as central to the toxicity. Both molecular docking and DARTS assays confirmed a direct interaction between alpha-AMA and GSTA1. Mechanistically, alpha-AMA activated the NRF2 pathway, leading to upregulated GSTA1 expression. Paradoxically, GSTA1 silencing alleviated toxicity. This detrimental effect was mediated through GSTA1-driven depletion of cellular glutathione (GSH), resulting in reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. CONCLUSION: This study unveils a novel mechanism where alpha-AMA hijacks the NRF2-GSTA1 antioxidant axis, transforming GSTA1 from a detoxifier into a key perpetrator of hepatotoxicity via GSH depletion, ROS overproduction. GSTA1 emerges as a promising direct therapeutic target and potential diagnostic biomarker for alpha-AMA poisoning, highlighting a critical direction for future research.
abstract_zh: 目的：α-鹅膏蕈碱（alpha-Amanitin, alpha-AMA）是致命蘑菇的主要毒素，通过加剧氧化应激诱导严重肝损伤。谷胱甘肽S-转移酶A1（Glutathione S-transferase A1, GSTA1）作为一种关键的肝脏抗氧化酶，在此过程中发挥的作用尚不明确。方法：建立alpha-AMA诱导肝损伤的小鼠模型。通过血清生化指标（ALT、AST、T-BIL）和组织病理学（H&E染色）评估肝脏损伤。检测氧化应激标志物（SOD、CAT、MDA）。采用整合转录组学和代谢组学识别关键通路。利用分子对接和药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability, DARTS）实验评估alpha-AMA与GSTA1之间的相互作用。在HUH7细胞中通过siRNA敲低和功能拯救实验进一步剖析体外机制。结果：alpha-AMA引起显著肝损伤，表现为血清标志物升高、组织病理学恶化及氧化应激增加（SOD/CAT降低，MDA升高）。多组学分析将GSTA1和谷胱甘肽代谢确定为其毒性的核心。分子对接和DARTS实验均证实alpha-AMA与GSTA1之间存在直接相互作用。机制上，alpha-AMA激活NRF2通路，导致GSTA1表达上调。矛盾的是，GSTA1沉默减轻了毒性。这种有害效应通过GSTA1驱动的细胞谷胱甘肽（GSH）耗竭介导，导致活性氧（ROS）积累。结论：本研究揭示了一种新机制，其中alpha-AMA劫持NRF2-GSTA1抗氧化轴，通过GSH耗竭和ROS过度产生，将GSTA1从解毒剂转变为肝毒性的关键促成者。GSTA1成为alpha-AMA中毒的有前景的直接治疗靶点和潜在诊断生物标志物，为未来研究指明了关键方向。
